# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Context & Assumptions
- Old and new billing systems run in parallel (dual-run) for the duration of the migration.
- Migration unit = one user account, including payment methods, invoice history, active subscriptions/entitlements, and dunning state.
- A "batch" is migrated via a reversible cutover: user's billing reads/writes are switched to the new system; the old system record is frozen (read-only) but **not removed**.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (0.5% of users, ~200 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full parallel-run reconciliation against the old system for 30 consecutive days on synthetic/shadow traffic (100% of live transactions mirrored, zero unexplained discrepancies), and rollback tooling has been tested end-to-end in staging.

**Population:** Internal employee accounts + opted-in low-risk users (monthly plans, no active disputes, single currency, no enterprise contracts).

**Duration:** 2 weeks minimum before proceeding.

## Phase 2: Early Adopters (10% of users, ~4,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full duration with zero Sev-1/Sev-2 billing incidents, invoice accuracy ≥99.99% against reconciliation, and support ticket rate for migrated cohort no higher than baseline ±10%.

**Population:** Broadened to include annual-plan users and multiple currencies, still excluding enterprise/custom-contract accounts and accounts with active payment disputes.

**Duration:** 3 weeks minimum, with weekly go/no-go review.

## Phase 3: General Availability (60% of users, ~24,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 metrics stable for 2 consecutive weeks, finance sign-off on revenue reconciliation, customer support fully trained and staffed for expected ticket volume, and automated rollback tested against a Phase-2-scale batch.

**Population:** All remaining standard accounts, migrated in daily or twice-weekly sub-batches (e.g., 5% increments) rather than as one bulk push.

**Duration:** 4–6 weeks.

## Phase 4: Complex & High-Risk Accounts (remaining ~29.5%, ~11,800 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete with cumulative billing-accuracy metrics within SLA, and each enterprise/custom-contract account has an individually reviewed migration plan signed off by account management.

**Population:** Enterprise contracts, custom pricing, accounts with active disputes/refunds in progress, and any accounts that failed earlier eligibility checks.

**Note:** This is the final batch of user migration. Decommissioning, disabling, or deleting the old billing system is explicitly **out of scope for this phase** and must occur only in a distinct, subsequent decommissioning phase after a full parallel-run soak period (minimum 60 days) post-Phase-4 completion, with data archival and audit sign-off completed first.

---

## Halt / Rollback Metrics

- **Automatic halt:** If invoice discrepancy rate (new vs. old system reconciliation) exceeds **0.1%** of transactions in any rolling 24-hour window, halt the current phase immediately and freeze further batch migrations pending root-cause analysis.
- Additional halt triggers: failed-payment rate for migrated cohort increases by more than 25% relative to pre-migration baseline; any Sev-1 billing incident (e.g., duplicate charges, incorrect tax calculation) affecting more than 10 users.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or missed charges during dual-run due to both systems attempting to bill the same invoice cycle | Implement an idempotent billing lock keyed by account ID so only the system of record for that account can trigger a charge, verified by pre-migration and post-migration reconciliation jobs | Billing Platform Engineering Lead
RISK: Data mapping errors for complex pricing (proration, discounts, tax rules) causing incorrect invoice amounts for enterprise accounts | Require manual review and test-invoice generation for every enterprise account before migration, with finance sign-off per account | Finance Systems Manager
RISK: Customer support volume spikes beyond capacity during General Availability phase, delaying resolution of billing complaints | Stagger GA into daily sub-batches sized to support team capacity, and pre-train support staff with a dedicated billing-migration runbook and escalation path | Customer Support Operations Manager
RISK: Rollback of a batch fails or is only partially reversible, leaving some users in an inconsistent billing state | Test full rollback procedure at each phase's scale before that phase begins, and require read-only freeze (not deletion) of old-system records so restoration is always possible | Site Reliability Engineering Lead
RISK: Payment method tokenization mismatch between old and new payment processors causes failed recurring charges | Run a token-migration validation step per batch that confirms a successful $0 authorization on the new system before the cutover completes | Payments Integration Lead

PHASES: 4
